analysis.title: Guess Who Just Hit Another All-Time High
key_insights: Europe's STOXX 600 closed at a record and the DAX also hit highs. The region's lack of AI exposure is now being framed as a diversification benefit.
Goldman (GIR) expects investors to increasingly return to Europe for AI diversification.
Goldman forecasts STOXX 600 EPS growth of 18% in 2026, 7% in 2027 and 5% in 2028.
BofA notes Europe has had a rare period of supportive earnings trends relative to the US.
US FCF yield has been weighed down by capex spending, while European FCF yield remains high (Datastream chart).
European High and Stable Margin companies are breaking out (Marquee).
Europe's valuation discount to the US remains significant but is around the narrowest since 2019 (BofA).
Goldman says the relief rally in French domestics looks premature relative to still challenging credit conditions.
Hedge fund net exposure to Europe is above the 90th percentile.
Morgan Stanley says positioning has recovered to pre-Iran levels, with an estimated ~$200B gap to cycle highs remaining and CTAs projected to buy ~$3B a day over the next week.
JPM says relative EU vs US flows are +1.5z over the past 1-3 months, but relative positioning is only back to neutral, leaving room for more.
earnings_insights: Goldman (GIR) forecast: STOXX 600 EPS growth of 18% in 2026, 7% in 2027, 5% in 2028 (forecast, not reported).
BofA: Europe has seen a rare period of supportive earnings trends relative to the US.
risk_factors: Positioning is already high among hedge funds (above 90th percentile net exposure), which limits fresh buying from that cohort.
French domestic relief rally may be premature given challenging credit conditions (Goldman).
The Market Ear closes with a note that the investor inflows into Europe tend not to last.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects a return to the region for AI diversification, STOXX 600 EPS growth of 18% in 2026, high FCF yield, breaking-out stable-margin names, and a valuation discount that is still significant. JPM says relative positioning is only back to neutral, and MS sees a ~$200B gap to cycle highs with CTA buying ahead.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds are already above the 90th percentile net exposure, and Goldman calls the French domestics relief rally premature given challenging credit conditions. The discount to the US is near its narrowest since 2019.

theme_stances.key_argument: Europe's lack of AI exposure now serves as diversification, with EPS growth, yield, margins and a valuation discount supporting inflows.
theme_stances.evidence: investors will increasingly return to the region for much-needed AI diversification
